why: A caller waiting on an agent names the state it is waiting for, and the window answers when a watched pane is in it. The question this pins is what 'in it' means, because the window paints five words and two of them describe one agent: `done` is `idle` on a pane nobody has looked at. A wait that took the words literally would depend on where somebody's cursor was.

cases.name: a state counts as itself
cases.why: The ordinary case. A caller waiting for `blocked` is answered by a blocked pane.

cases.name: an idle pane counts as idle
cases.why: An agent that finished on a pane somebody was looking at.

cases.name: a done pane counts as idle
cases.why: `done` is an idle nobody has seen, which is a fact about the window rather than the agent. An integrator waiting for a worker to finish waits for `idle`, and whether the worker's pane was on screen when it finished must not decide whether the wait ever ends.

cases.name: an idle pane does not count as done
cases.why: The reverse is not the same claim. A caller asking for `done` is asking which finished agents nobody has noticed, and one somebody has looked at is not among them.

cases.name: a working pane does not count as idle
cases.why: The wait this whole concept exists for: an agent still working has not finished.

cases.name: a blocked pane does not count as idle
cases.why: Blocked is stopped and waiting on somebody, which is not finished. A caller who wants either names both.

cases.name: an unknown pane counts as unknown
cases.why: A plain shell reads `unknown`, so a caller waiting for a harness to exit and leave its shell behind can wait for this.
